The test image shows a tomato plant that has been pulled from the ground. Key features:
- Whole plant is wilted and collapsed
- Main stems are pale/bleached tan-white in color
- Some brown lesions on stems
- Roots visible and appear brown/rotted
- Leaves are wilted with some browning

Now let me check the part index to narrow candidates.

The image shows a whole plant with stem/root involvement. Top candidates from whole_plant + stem categories: Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot, Southern_Blight, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Verticillium_Wilt, Bacterial_Wilt.

The bleached/pale stems and plant collapse suggest Sclerotinia or Southern_Blight. Let me view one reference per class starting with top candidates.
Sclerotinia root reference is very similar to the test image — plants pulled from ground, pale/bleached stems, visible root rot. Let me continue checking other classes.

Based on all 16 views, here is my analysis:

**Test image features:**
- Tomato plants uprooted and laid on a dark surface (black plastic mulch)
- Stems are pale/bleached tan-white — very distinctive
- Brown lesions on stems
- Visible root rot (brown roots)
- Plant fully collapsed/dead

**Key comparisons:**
- `Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot/root/Bugwood_19.jpg`: Very strong visual match — uprooted plants on a surface, pale bleached stems, root rot, collapsed plant
- `Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot/stem/Bugwood_21.jpg`: Shows characteristic bleached/whitened stem at soil line with black sclerotia — matches the pale stem coloration
- `Southern_Blight`: Stems are dark/brown, not bleached — doesn't match
- `Bacterial_Wilt`, `Southern_Bacterial_Wilt`: Stems remain green during wilt — doesn't match
- `Gray_Mold`, `Anthracnose`, `Rhizopus_Soft_Rots`: All microscopic or clearly different presentations

The pale/bleached stem coloration combined with root rot and plant collapse matches Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot most closely.
